items.actClause:
AN ACT in relation to requiring the commissioner of motor vehicles to enter
into an agreement with the Republic of China (Taiwan) for reciprocity of
driver licenses
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4329                 Revised 2/23/2023

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to requiring the commissioner of motor vehicles to
enter into an agreement with the Republic of China (Taiwan) for reci-
procity of driver licenses

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would require the commissioner of motor vehicles to enter into
a driver license reciprocity agreement with the Republic of China
(Taiwan).

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: This bill requires New York State and the Republic of China
(Taiwan) to enter into a drivers' license reciprocity agreement.

Section 2: The parties will enter into an agreement for reciprocity in
issuing driver licenses to citizens from NYS residing in Taiwan and to
holders of valid Taiwanese driver licenses lawfully residing in NYS.
Both parties will agree on the reciprocal provision for issuance and
skills. Both parties shall agree that a holder of a valid, unexpired
license residing of the state of New York residing in the Republic of
China (Taiwan), will be able to exchange such license for a Taiwanese
driver license at a normal conversion fee, without being required to
pass the theoretical and practical test and vice versa.  If the license
is expired, all tests will be required.

Section 3: Both parties shall agree on: 1. Each party shall provide
sample of driver licenses issued at time of the agreement and definition
of all classes of driver licenses, notations and restrictions. 2. This
agreement only applies to holders of unrestricted driver licenses aged
18 or older and shall not apply to applications for enhanced licenses,
real ID's or driver licenses for the operation of a commercial motor
vehicle or motorcycle 3. The standards, rules and regulations shall be
the same as for any resident of the state of NY and/or the Republic of
China (Taiwan). 4.  Each side shall agree to verify that the driver
license is still valid in the state it was issued.

Section 4: This agreement shall be signed by both the commissioner of
motor vehicles of NYS and the Director General of the Taipei Economic
and Cultural Representative office in the United States and may be
canceled or revoked in writing by either party at any time and for any
reason, with three months notice, provided that notification is sent to
the address provided by the parties in agreement.

Section 5: The commissioner of motor vehicles shall draft the agreement
and present such agreement to the Director General of the Taipei Econom-
ic Cultural Office in New York within 90 days of the date this shall
have become law.

Section 6: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:


Currently, there are 38 states and territories - AL, AZ, AR, CO, DE, FL,
GA, HI, ID, IN, IA, KS, KY, LA, MD, MA, MN, MS, MT, NV, NJ, NM, OH, OK,
OR, PA, PR, RI, SC, TN, TX, VT, VI, VA, WA, WV, WI, WY- that have
entered into such agreements with Taiwan. By entering into a driver
license reciprocity agreement, New York State's Department of Transpor-
tation and the Republic of China (Taiwan), through the Ministry of
Transportation and Communications, would agree to recognize and exchange
valid driver's licenses issue by the other's jurisdiction. The benefit
for New York State for Taiwanese businessmen, researchers, students and
so on to get a New York State license would be the increase of mobility
in the State which in turn is a direct benefit to economic development
of New York State. The licensing and skill requirements necessary to
become licensed in each jurisdiction is comparable - ensuring that
Taiwanese license holders would meet the same rules and regulations and
high standards as New York driver license holders and vice versa. Thus,
guaranteeing the safety of our roadways.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S. 6649-A of 2022: Amended and Recommitted to Transportation;

S. 6649-A of 2021: Referred to Transportation;

S. 2951 of 2020: New Bill, Referred to Transportation

 
LOCAL FISCAL AND FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

AN ACT in relation to authorizing the commissioner of motor vehicles to enter

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4329A

SPONSOR: SEPULVEDA
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act in relation to authorizing the commissioner of motor vehicles to
enter into reciprocity agreements with other states, countries, prov-
inces or territories that issue driver licenses

 
PURPOSE:

This bill would allow the commissioner of motor vehicles to enter into
driver license reciprocity agreements.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: This bill allows New York State to enter into drivers'
license reciprocity agreements with other states, countries, provinces,
or territories.

Section 2: The parties will enter into an agreement for reciprocity in
issuing driver licenses to citizens from NYS residing in other states,
countries, provinces, or territories, as well as holders of valid driver
licenses lawfully residing in NYS from other states, countries, prov-
inces, or territories. Both parties will agree on the reciprocal
provision for issuance and skills. Both parties shall agree that a hold-
er of a valid, unexpired license of the state of New York residing in
the other states, countries, provinces, or territories, will be able to
exchange such license at a normal conversion fee, without being required
to pass the theoretical and practical test and vice versa. If the
license is expired, all tests will be required.

Section 3: Both parties shall agree on: 1. Each party shall provide
sample of driver licenses issued at time of the agreement and definition
of all classes of driver licenses, notations and restrictions. 2. This
agreement only applies to holders of unrestricted driver licenses aged
18 or older and shall not apply to applications for enhanced licenses,
real ID's or driver licenses for the operation of a commercial motor
vehicle or motorcycle. 3. The standards, rules and regulations shall be
the same as for any resident of the state of NY and/or the other state,
country, province, or territory.

Section 4: This agreement shall be signed by both the commissioner of
motor vehicles of NYS and an official with legal authority of the
respective state, country, province, or territory. It may be canceled or
revoked in writing by either party at any time and for any reason, with
three months' notice, provided that notification is sent to the address
provided by the parties in agreement.

Section 5: The commissioner of motor vehicles shall report to the gover-
nor, the temporary President of the Senate, and the Speaker of the
Assembly within one year of enactment and annually thereafter.

Section 6: Effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation would allow great flexibility for New Yorkers working
abroad who want to obtain drivers licenses in the countries they are
working in as will business people from other countries residing in New
York. For example - Currently, there are 38 states and territories - AL,
AZ, AR, CO, DE, FL, GA, HI, ID, IA, KS, KY, LA, MD, MA, MN, MS, MT, NV,
NJ, NM, OH, OK, OR, PA, PR, RI, SC, TN, TX, VT, VI, VA, WA, WV, WI, WY-
that have entered into such agreements with Taiwan. By entering into a
driver license reciprocity agreement, New York State's Department of
Transportation and the Republic of China (Taiwan), through the Ministry
of Transportation and Communications, would agree to recognize and
exchange valid driver's licenses issued by the other's jurisdiction. The
benefit for New York State for Taiwanese businessmen, researchers,
students and so on to get a New York State license would be the increase
of mobility in the State which in turn is a direct benefit to economic
development of New York State. The licensing and skill requirements
necessary to become licensed in each jurisdiction is comparable - ensur-
ing that Taiwanese license holders would meet the same rules and regu-
lations and high standards as New York driver license holders and vice
versa. Thus, guaranteeing the safety of our roadways.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S. 6649- A of 2022: Amended and Recommitted to Transportation;

S. 6649- A of 2021: Referred to Transportation;

S. 2951 of 2020: New Bill, Referred to Transportation

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
